key: And the LORD smote the king, so that he was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a house set apart. And Jotham the king’s son was over the household, judging the people of the land.
s: At the head of a chapter of conspiracies in Israel, Judah’s Azariah does right yet is stricken; Metzudat David, on 15:5, reads the ‘house set apart’ as release from the toil of governing, kingship counting, as the sages say, as servitude, and Rashi, on 15:5, as a house among the graves, the dead being called free.

evidence.words: בבית החפשית. רצה לומר: עזב הנהגת המלכות, והיה חפשי מזה העמל, וכמו שאמרו רבותינו ז״ל שהמלכות יחשב לעבדות, לפי רוב העמל … בְּבֵית הַחָפְשִׁית. עָשָׂה לוֹ בַּיִת בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת, כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אֲמַר בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי
evidence.gloss: Metzudat David: “In the house of freedom”: that is, he left the governing of the kingdom and was free of that toil, as our rabbis said that kingship is reckoned servitude, for the greatness of its toil. Rashi: “In the house of freedom”: he made himself a house in the cemetery, as it is said of the dead, “free” (the dead are called free).

reason: CORRECTED for both clarity faults, which hold. (1) The opening participle dangled onto Azariah; the context clause now reads ‘At the head of a chapter of conspiracies in Israel, Judah’s Azariah does right yet is stricken’ (day.js: 15:1 to 15:3 Azariah begins and does right, 15:5 stricken; conspiracies at 15:10, 15:25, 15:30). (2) Rashi’s reading lacked its ground: re-opened packet.js tanakh 123 --verse 15.5, Rashi on בְּבֵית הַחָפְשִׁית: עָשָׂה לוֹ בַּיִת בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת, כְּמָה דְּאַתְּ אֲמַר בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי, so ‘the dead being called free’ is his own stated reason and now carries the link from ‘set apart’ (Hebrew ‘house of freedom’) to the graves. ‘He made himself’ dropped for length; the house is still his. Metzudat David unchanged and re-found (עזב הנהגת המלכות, והיה חפשי מזה העמל ... המלכות יחשב לעבדות).
